13.5 Tangential and Normal Components of Acceleration

If you are traveling along a space curve, the Cartesian i, j, and k coordinate system for representing the vectors describing your motion is not truly relevant to you. What is mean- ingful instead are the vectors representative of your forward direction (the unit tangent vector T), the direction in which your path is turning (the unit normal vector N), and the tendency of your motion to “twist” out of the plane created by these vectors in the direc- tion perpendicular to this plane (defined by the unit binormal vector B = T * N). Expressing the acceleration vector along the curve as a linear combination of this TNB frame of mutually orthogonal unit vectors traveling with the motion (Figure 13.23) is par- ticularly revealing of the nature of the path and motion along it.
